Ellen — great to meet yesterday. As discussed, attaching a draft Mutual Action Plan (pulseiq_map_draft_v3.xlsx) that ties evaluation milestones to a close timeline. Two things we want to lock down early from a cost perspective so your engineering and procurement teams can validate:

- Tokens / $ assumptions: we put a conservative baseline of 1,800,000 request tokens / month (50% prompts, 50% generated) and modeled at 3.2k tokens / USD for the pinned model. Need confirmation of expected request shape and any heavy-generation flows.
- Caching & batching: our default recommendation is prefix caching for the 30% repeated prompts and dynamic batching up to 32 seqs for latency-sensitive routes. That reduces effective tokens by ~18% in our model; want to surface any workload constraints.

Quick asks for your team:
1) Can you share the token/sample trace (anonymized) for a typical week? PulseIQ sent a small sample earlier; attaching token_mix_samples.json would help if you have a broader slice.
2) Any hard SLOs for p95 latency on API calls? We used 500ms p95 in the workbook but happy to adjust.
3) Procurement cadence: are there contract gating dates we should aim for to hit a July close?

If easiest, we can do a 30-min call Thurs to walk the econ tab with your eng and procurement.

Thanks — Mina

Copying my notes from the econ tab so we're aligned before Thurs: 

1) Token mix assumptions — Workbook baseline: 50/50 prompt/response tokens, median sequence length 512. If PulseIQ has longer generation modes (chat summaries), we should model a 70/30 split and re-run.
2) Batching impact — we estimate 18-22% token cost reduction at 32-way batching for stable request shapes; for high-variance (many short prompts + occasional long) the benefit drops to ~8-10%. Need Rajiv's trace to quantify.
3) Caching — prefix/KV cache assumptions: we modeled 30% hit rate. If PulseIQ can use a stronger deterministic prompt structure (e.g., canonical patient-search queries) we could push to 45% which materially changes unit cost.
4) Fallback model plan — recommend a warm fallback to a cheaper quantized variant for non-critical/low-quality routes. This nets ~25% tokens/$ improvement for those routes but requires explicit routing policy in the MAP.

Action items (internal):
- Ben: draft a one-page sensitivity table (tokens/$ vs hit rate vs batching) for the Thurs call.
- Jordan: prepare a short note on routing & fallback policy implications for SLOs.

I can present the econ tab. Mina, please confirm calendar invite time.

— Karthik
Senior Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference

Adding the sensitivity table draft (attached as inline summary). Key short takeaways to bring to PulseIQ: 

- If token hit rate = 30% and batching benefit = 10% => effective tokens/$ improves by 12%. 
- If hit rate = 45% and batching = 25% => effective tokens/$ improves by 34% (this is optimistic but achievable with canonical prompts).
- Model quantization to 4-bit for fallback reduces cost per token ~20% but increases latency variance; recommend fallback only for async/low-SLO routes.

I'll attach the spreadsheet to the invite and include the sensitivity charts so Ellen's team can eyeball ranges quickly.
